Bragg-peak segmentation on peaknet10k: proof report

Six segmentation statements (peaknet_baseline, hf_segformer, hf_upernet, lucid_segformer, lucid_unet, best_model) trained on the shared run-level split and evaluated on the whole test split (1529 images) with the shared metric code (test peak F1 at 3 px tolerance; pixel IoU second). Every figure on this page was rendered on S3DF from real checkpoints, predictions and logs; nothing was captured on any other machine.

S3DF evidence: jobs, training curves, logs, independent read-back

Findings

  • 01:20-01:33 PST: every first training attempt died at the first convolution with CUDNN_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED. Cause: CUDA-13 wheels in the shared venv had overwritten torch's cu12 cuDNN/NCCL/cuSPARSELt (not GPU hardware). Fixed by reinstalling the cu12 pins (h1, log runs/h1/envfix/uv.log); runs relaunched 01:34-01:38. The FAILED/CANCELLED steps in the sacct capture are these attempts.
  • Labelled peaks are tiny (median 1-2 px, 4-35 peaks per 1920x1920 image; positive pixel fraction about 1e-6 to 1e-5). Models therefore use full-resolution heads (PixelShuffle or full-res decoders) and peak-centred training crops.

  • This version of the page was built while the first training runs were still in progress; per-model test results, overlays and the independent re-evaluation are added as each model statement lands on main.

All PNGs are rendered on S3DF (sdfiana025 login node reading the shared filesystem; Slurm job steps on sdfada013 for model inference) and copied byte-for-byte with ops/fetch_bin.sh. Durable copies: /sdf/data/lcls/ds/prj/prjcwang31/results/peaknet-seg-sprint/figures/h8/proof/.
